html:
The Italo-Turkish War was fought in 1911 and 1912 between Italy and the Ottoman Empire, when Italy invaded the Ottoman provinces of Tripolitania and Cyrenaica, which it then joined as Libya.

Italy expected an easy war but met hard resistance from Ottoman officers and local Arab and Berber fighters. On 1 November 1911 an Italian pilot dropped bombs on Ottoman troops near Tripoli, the first air raid in history. The Ottomans gave up the provinces in the Treaty of Ouchy in October 1912.

Inland, the Senussi kept up the fight for twenty years, led by Omar Mukhtar. The war also showed the Balkan states that the Ottomans were weak, and they attacked in October 1912. See also Italy.
sum: The Italo-Turkish War was fought in 1911 and 1912 between Italy and the Ottoman Empire, when Italy invaded the Ottoman provinces of Tripolitania and Cyrenaica, which it then joined as Libya.
